name: createConfluenceContent
description:
Create a new Confluence page, blog post, live doc, whiteboard, database,
embed, smart link, or folder.

Before choosing body.format or authoring a body, call getContentFormatGuide through execute with
name=getContentFormatGuide and inputs={toolName}. Use createConfluencePage
for pages, blog posts, and live docs; createConfluenceWhiteboard for
whiteboards; or createConfluenceDatabase for databases.

Space instructions describe how to author content in a Confluence space.
Apply relevant guidance to the content you create or update. Follow this
decision rule:
1. Before authoring, call getConfluenceSpace for the target space unless
   getConfluenceContent returned metadata.hasSpaceInstructions=false for
   content in that space. If getConfluenceSpace already returned for the
   same cloudId and space during the current task, reuse its
   spaceInstructions and do not call it again.
2. When the value is true or unknown and instructions have not been
   loaded, you must call getConfluenceSpace once before authoring through
   execute with name=getConfluenceSpace, top-level cloudId, and
   inputs={spaceIdOrKey}.
3. Apply any returned spaceInstructions. If a successful response omits
   them, no instructions are configured; author with defaults and do not
   block.

After a successful getConfluenceSpace call, do not make a separate
getConfluenceSpaceInstructions call.

cloudId.description: Site UUID or Jira/Confluence URL for this operation's Atlassian site. cloudId is never silently auto-resolved or reused for you — call getAccessibleAtlassianResources ONCE per session, cache the returned cloudId, and pass it explicitly on this and every subsequent call, since most operations need it. `execute` and its read/write/destructive variants strictly require it for cloudId-scoped operations and fail without it. Not needed for cloudId-less operations (e.g. Bitbucket), which ignore this field.

parent.description:
Parent destination for the new content.

Use { "spaceId": "<numeric-space-id>" } to create at the homepage / sidebar root.
Use { "spaceId": "<numeric-space-id>", "parentContentId": "<numeric-content-id>" }
to create under an existing content item.
Use { "parentContentId": "<numeric-content-id>" } when the parent content ID
should be resolved to its space before creation.
Use { "parentContentUrl": "<confluence-content-url>" } when the parent
content URL should be resolved before creation.

Supported parentContentUrl paths include /pages/{id}, /blog/{id},
/whiteboard/{id}, /database/{id}, and /folder/{id}.

If the destination is described only by space key or title, resolve it first
to one of the supported parent shapes above.

contentType.description:
Type of content to create. One of: page, live_doc, blogpost, whiteboard,
database, embed, smart_link, folder, slide.

title.description: Title for the new content. 1-255 characters.

body.description:
Before composing this body, follow the space-instruction decision rule in the tool
description. Reuse known instruction state and do not repeat the space lookup per write.
Body content. For whiteboard and database it is technically optional, but only omit it
when the user explicitly asked for an empty/blank board or database. Never omit body as a
fallback because you could not load the authoring guidance — load it first via
getContentFormatGuide through the generic operation runner (execute) as
name=getContentFormatGuide, inputs={toolName} (createConfluencePage /
createConfluenceWhiteboard / createConfluenceDatabase), then build a real body.
A blank whiteboard
(no shapes, stickies, connectors, or layout) is almost never the intended result.
For doc types (page, live_doc, blogpost): format is html or markdown, value is the content string.
Markdown is for simple text; use HTML when richer structure would improve the document.
For embed and smart_link: format must be url, value must be the URL to embed (e.g. https://example.com/design).
For whiteboard: format must be svg and value must be the complete initial SVG document with root width, height, and viewBox.
For database: format must be csv and value must be the complete initial CSV payload.
For a synced (Smart) Folder (contentType=folder): format must be url and value must be the
https URL of the external Google Drive, OneDrive, or SharePoint folder to sync from.
Requires the confluence_smart_folders_milestone_1 experiment; otherwise the create
returns FEATURE_NOT_ENABLED.
Do not pass patches, edit envelopes, or context on create.
Omit for a plain folder (no sync source) and for slide.

draft.description:
If true, create the content as a draft instead of publishing it. Only
supported when contentType is page or blogpost.

private.description:
If true, the created content is private to the caller: only the
creator has view and edit access. Supported for page, live_doc,
blogpost, whiteboard, database, and folder, including creation at the
homepage / sidebar root. Private creation is not supported for embed, smart_link, or slide.
This sets General access to VIEW_RESTRICTED and gives the creator one
Specific access grant, update (Can edit), which already includes
read/view. Do not add a separate read grant for the creator.
Omit or pass false for default visibility.

contentWidth.description:
Optional page width for doc types only: page, live_doc, and blogpost.
Omit unless the user explicitly requests a width; omission creates a
narrow page. Do not infer wide or max from body content or layout.
Accepted values are narrow, wide, and max.
Non-doc content types do not support this field.
